quote: I know now, I understand at last, Constantine, that for us, whether we write or act, it is not the honour and glory of which I have dreamt that is important, it is the strength to endure.
source: Anton Chekhov, The Sea-Gull, Act IV, to Treplieff (Nina) (trans. Marian Fell, 1912)
speaker: Nina
note: The wording is Marian Fell’s, page 220 of the 1912 Scribner volume. The proposal placed it in Nina’s last speech. It is not: it closes her long speech about the stage, and she speaks twice more before she runs out. The locator now says only Act IV, to Treplieff.

evidence.where: Archive.org full-text OCR of the Cornell copy of Plays by Anton Tchekoff (title leaf: Marian Fell; Charles Scribner’s Sons; Copyright 1912, Published September 1912), fetched this run; sentence verbatim on the page headed 220 THE SEA-GULL ACT IV. Cross-checked against Project Gutenberg ebook 1754, lines 2490 to 2493, identical, and read on to the end of the scene to count Nina’s speeches.
evidence.edition: Plays by Anton Tchekoff, trans. Marian Fell (New York: Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1912)
evidence.locator: The Sea-Gull, Act IV, p. 220, Nina to Treplieff, the sentence before One must know how to bear one’s cross, and one must have faith; her third speech from the end, not her last

reason: The refutation is right and narrow: the sentence is verbatim in Fell 1912 and in Gutenberg 1754, but Nina has two further speeches after Treplieff answers, so “her last speech” was a false locator. With that claim dropped the line is sound: a whole sentence, not shipped, Chekhov at one in the year and none in March, not banned, on theme.
